title: [bug] Tauri fails to build on Fedora 41 (Failed to get GBM device)
body: I created a default React app with `npm create tauri-app@latest` on Fedora 41. When I run `npm run tauri dev`, the window appears with an empty screen and the terminal reports `Failed to get GBM device`. I attached a screenshot and the development log.

symptoms_visible: My default React Tauri app opens an empty window on Fedora 41, and `npm run tauri dev` prints `Failed to get GBM device`.
N0.label: N0 empty window and GBM error reported

symptoms_visible: The default Tauri app still opens with an empty screen in my standard-install virtual machines.
N1.label: N1 test setup clarified

symptoms_visible: The app still shows an empty window even though Fedora already has webkit2gtk 4.1 version 2.46.4 installed.
N2.label: N2 installed rendering package version established

symptoms_visible: When I launch the app with `WEBKIT_DISABLE_COMPOSITING_MODE=1`, it runs and the window is no longer empty.
N3.label: N3 launch command verified

symptoms_visible: The Tauri window renders when the WebKit compositing-mode environment variable is set for the running application.
N_terminal.label: terminal runtime workaround adopted

question_patterns: What kind of machine and display setup are you testing on?
Does this happen on physical hardware or in a virtual machine, and did you use a standard installation image?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: All my tests were done on virtual machines using standard ISO installations.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: This only happens on my physical Nvidia machine under Wayland; the same project works in a standard virtual machine.
I reproduced it in two different virtual machines installed from the standard Fedora ISO.

edges.comment: Issue c1-c2, reporter's systems only: a maintainer asked whether this was a Wayland and Nvidia setup; the reporter answered that the tests used VMs with standard ISO installations and did not claim a specific GPU or display protocol.

question_patterns: Which version of the relevant web-rendering package is installed on Fedora?
Can you check the installed 4.1 web-rendering package version?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Fedora reports that `webkit2gtk4.1-2.46.4-1.fc41.x86_64` is already installed.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I have an older package installed, and updating it makes the window render normally.
The installed Fedora package is another 2.46.4 build with a different Fedora release suffix.

edges.comment: Issue c1-c2, reporter's Fedora VM: an older WebKitGTK version was raised as a possibility, after which the reporter supplied the installed 2.46.4 Fedora package version.

question_patterns: Could you run the command I shared and report whether the window renders?
Please launch the development app once with the suggested command and tell me what you see.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Running `WEBKIT_DISABLE_COMPOSITING_MODE=1 npm run tauri dev` actually fixed the issue for running the app. Can I configure that automatically instead of adding it to the command each time?

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The window remains empty and the same GBM error appears when I launch it with the suggested command.
The suggested command fixes the window in both of my standard-install virtual machines.

edges.comment: Issue c1-c2, reporter's systems: this is a handler-initiated launch test. The reporter confirmed only the observable result and then volunteered that they wanted the setting applied automatically.

solution.intent: Treat the empty window as an upstream WebKitGTK graphics-runtime problem and apply the already verified WebKit compositing workaround at application startup, before constructing the Tauri builder.
solution.concrete_example: For a built application, set the runtime variable before `tauri::Builder::default()` in `lib.rs` or `main.rs`, for example: `std::env::set_var("WEBKIT_DISABLE_COMPOSITING_MODE", "1");`. A maintainer also suggested trying `WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER=1`, with the already verified compositing variable as the fallback if that is insufficient.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter established that the current Fedora WebKitGTK package was installed and that disabling WebKit compositing restored rendering. Classifying the failure as an upstream WebKitGTK graphics-runtime problem is the maintainers' diagnosis; the thread does not establish a more precise underlying defect or confirm Wayland plus Nvidia.

edges.comment: Issue c0-c3, opening reporter's runtime problem only: maintainers classified the white-window/GBM behavior as upstream and gave an in-process way to set the runtime variable before the Tauri builder. The later AppImage bundling failure beginning at c4 is explicitly described in c5 as unrelated and is excluded as a separate problem.

satisfaction_conditions: Must diagnose the opening empty-window and `Failed to get GBM device` behavior at the level established by the thread: an upstream WebKitGTK graphics-runtime issue, without claiming that Wayland plus Nvidia was confirmed.
Must ground the recommendation in the reported evidence that Fedora already had webkit2gtk 4.1 version 2.46.4 and that launching with `WEBKIT_DISABLE_COMPOSITING_MODE=1` restored the window.

Must recommend applying the verified runtime environment workaround before `tauri::Builder` when an automatic in-app setting is desired, rather than treating an application-startup variable as a build-time setting.
Must not attribute the opening runtime failure solely to an outdated WebKitGTK package, because the reporter had version 2.46.4 installed.
Must ask the reporter to verify that the window renders with the runtime setting and must not declare resolution without the reporter's successful launch result.

persona_hint.experience_level: Developer able to scaffold React and Tauri projects, edit Rust startup code, inspect installed Linux packages, and test builds across standard-install virtual machines, but unfamiliar with the distinction between build-time and application-runtime environment variables.
persona_hint.communication_style: Cooperative and concrete; shares commands, package versions, source snippets, and logs; asks practical follow-up questions about making a working command-line workaround automatic.
